_comment: Archived Bengali-era retrieval baseline. Not applicable to the Hindi/Indic corpus; comparison and update command are disabled.
note: First baseline on the frozen 42-question set (10 original + 32 hand-verified, chunk-first; 50 gold chunks over 37 of the 48 papers). Supersedes the 10-question directional baseline. MRR is truncated at max(k_values), so it is MRR@10 here and rises to 0.584 when k=100 is scored - always quote it with its depth. Headline finding: recall@1 0.393 vs recall@20 0.869 means most gold material IS retrieved but ranked badly, so reranking is the main lever; but recall@100 0.940 leaves ~6% of gold chunks unreachable at any practical depth, which is a genuine coverage gap and revives the case for hybrid retrieval. The reranking-vs-coverage argument that follows from these numbers is recorded in docs/decisions/008. Added nDCG@k and bootstrap intervals. The 95% intervals are ~0.23-0.26 wide, an order of magnitude more than this file's +/-3% tolerance: that tolerance guards against a change in THIS measurement, and says nothing about how the figure would move on another 42 questions. Treat a reranker's absolute numbers accordingly and judge it on bootstrap_delta_ci over the same queries.

confidence_intervals_95._comment: Percentile bootstrap over queries, seeded. Width is how much each figure depends on WHICH 42 questions were asked. Compare two retrievers with bootstrap_delta_ci on the same questions, not by checking whether these overlap.
